concerns.text: The plan relies on a bundled placeholder CSV (`hea_placeholder.csv`) because no verified open‑source HEA dataset is available. This undermines external/construct validity – conclusions about the predictive power of ML for real HEAs cannot be supported by a synthetic placeholder.

Statistical power is not addressed: the Mann‑Whitney U test (Phase 2‑2.1) and Spearman correlation (Phase 2‑2.5) are performed without any justification of sample size or power analysis, risking type‑II errors especially when the novel set may be far smaller than the intended 5 000.

Uncertainty is quantified solely by ensemble variance and its correlation with convex‑hull distance. No calibration assessment (e.g., reliability diagrams, prediction interval coverage) is performed, so the variance may not be a valid uncertainty metric for the research question.

The Hold‑out Known set is created via deterministic element‑pair stratification (10 % of train). This split may still share compositional similarity with the training set, leading to leakage and confounding the extrapolation error measurement.

The correlation between variance and hull distance is computed in a PCA‑reduced descriptor space that was fit on the training data, potentially introducing a circularity that inflates the observed Spearman ρ, compromising construct validity.
